interviews.speaker: Kai Brüning
interviews.why: This is the process's own interview: it states the activity's impact grid (all 1s), RTO, MTPD and BCMS relevance.

owner.name: Kai Brüning
owner.quote: The systematic recording, management and control of all of a company's IT assets and configuration items (CIs), to ensure their integrity, traceability and dependencies over the whole life cycle. It is a support process, and its process owner is the head of IT service management.

mtpd.speaker: Kai Brüning
mtpd.reason: Stated by the process owner; consistent with the grid never reaching the threshold of 4.

rto.speaker: Kai Brüning
rto.reason: The owner's own recovery decision, carried as stated; an RTO past the last horizon over an MTPD past the last horizon is not a recovery gap.

rpo.reason: Nothing at all was said about RPO in the interview; proposed >168 h because CMDB/asset record data are rebuilt over the life cycle and no other process names this process as time-critical.

conflicts.about: MTPD: the grid (2025) gives no MTPD within horizons by the method's rule, the draft says >168 h

sides.claim: no MTPD within horizons (the method's rule over the grid, 2025)
sides.speaker: method

conflicts.why: The method derives the MTPD from the grid; the other figure is the thing to explain.

gaps.what: The interview names no sub-steps, no resources and no dependencies for the process, so evidence for what the activity needs (e.g. a CMDB/ITSM tool, Microsoft 365) and for any data-loss tolerance is missing.
gaps.ask: Which systems and roles does asset and configuration management depend on, and how much asset/CI data can be lost (RPO) before the process is impaired?
